question_en: In a double-blind trial, should the blind be broken to report a serious adverse reaction on an expedited basis?
question_es: En un ensayo doble ciego, ¿debe romperse el ciego para notificar de forma expeditiva una reacción adversa grave?
reference: When a serious adverse reaction is judged reportable on an expedited basis, ICH E2A recommends that the blind be broken only for that specific patient by the sponsor, even if the investigator has not broken it, and that the blind be maintained, when possible and appropriate, for those responsible for analysis and interpretation (e.g. biometrics personnel); retaining the blind has disadvantages, e.g. placebo and comparator cases are filed unnecessarily (ICH E2A §III.D, p.8).
notes: Held-out item (written after v4 was frozen). ICH E2A 'Managing Blinded Therapy Cases', p.8.

question_en: Do reactions to an active comparator or to placebo have to be reported on an expedited basis?
question_es: ¿Hay que notificar de forma expeditiva las reacciones a un comparador activo o al placebo?
reference: The sponsor decides whether active comparator reactions are reported to the other manufacturer and/or directly to the appropriate regulatory agencies, but must report them to one of the two; events associated with placebo will usually not satisfy the criteria for an ADR and therefore for expedited reporting (ICH E2A §III.E.1, p.9).
notes: Held-out item. ICH E2A 'Reactions Associated with Active Comparator or Placebo Treatment', p.9.

question_en: How should serious adverse events that occur after a patient has completed a clinical study be handled for expedited reporting?
question_es: ¿Cómo deben tratarse, a efectos de notificación expeditiva, los acontecimientos adversos graves que ocurren después de que el paciente haya terminado el estudio?
expected_keywords: study report|study reports|notificaciones del estudio|informes del estudio|casos del estudio
reference: Post-study serious adverse events are not routinely sought, but when an investigator reports them to the sponsor they should be regarded for expedited reporting purposes as though they were study reports; a causality assessment and determination of expectedness are needed to decide on expedited reporting (ICH E2A §III.E.3, p.9).
notes: Held-out item. ICH E2A 'Post-study Events', p.9.

question_en: What composition does ICH E6(R3) recommend for an IRB/IEC?
question_es: ¿Qué composición recomienda ICH E6(R3) para un IRB/IEC (comité de ética)?
reference: A reasonable number of members who collectively have the qualifications and experience to review the science, medical aspects and ethics of the trial; recommended: at least five members; at least one member whose primary area of interest is not in medical sciences; at least one member independent of the institution/investigator site. Only members independent of the investigator and sponsor should vote or give an opinion; a list of members and qualifications is maintained (ICH E6(R3) §1.3.1).

question_en: What qualifications does ICH E6(R3) require of an investigator?
question_es: ¿Qué cualificación exige ICH E6(R3) a un investigador?
reference: The investigator should be qualified by education, training and experience to assume responsibility for the proper conduct of the trial and provide evidence of such qualifications (ICH E6(R3) §2.1.1), and should be familiar with the appropriate use of the investigational product as described in the protocol, the current Investigator's Brochure, the product information and other sponsor information (§2.1.2).
notes: Held-out item. ICH E6(R3) §2.1.1-2.1.2, p.18 (investigator section, not Principle 2.1).

question_en: What types of monitoring does ICH E6(R3) describe, and how should the sponsor decide the extent of monitoring?
question_es: ¿Qué tipos de monitorización describe ICH E6(R3) y cómo debe decidir el promotor su alcance?
reference: Monitoring may be performed on-site and/or remotely and as centralised monitoring (a timely evaluation of accumulated data by qualified sponsor personnel such as data managers or biostatisticians); the sponsor determines the appropriate extent and nature of monitoring based on identified risks and factors such as the trial's objective, design and complexity; monitoring should be performed by persons not involved in the clinical conduct of the trial at the site (ICH E6(R3) §3.11.4, §3.11.4.2).

question_en: What must the investigator do about protocol deviations under ICH E6(R3)?
question_es: ¿Qué debe hacer el investigador con las desviaciones del protocolo según ICH E6(R3)?
reference: The investigator should document all protocol deviations, review them (including those communicated by the sponsor), and for important deviations explain them and implement appropriate measures to prevent recurrence (ICH E6(R3) §2.5.3); deviations from or changes to the protocol should not be initiated without prior IRB/IEC approval except where necessary to eliminate immediate hazards to participants (§1.4.7, §2.5.4).

question_en: What does the Declaration of Helsinki require about publishing research results?
question_es: ¿Qué exige la Declaración de Helsinki sobre la publicación de los resultados de la investigación?
expected_keywords: conflicts of interest|conflictos de interés|conflicto de intereses
reference: Researchers have a duty to make the results of research on human participants publicly available and are accountable for the timeliness, completeness and accuracy of their reports; negative and inconclusive as well as positive results must be published or otherwise made publicly available; sources of funding, institutional affiliations and conflicts of interest must be declared; reports of research not in accordance with the Declaration should not be accepted for publication (Declaration of Helsinki 2024 ¶36).

question_en: What does the Declaration of Helsinki say about consent for storing biological material and data for future research?
question_es: ¿Qué dice la Declaración de Helsinki sobre el consentimiento para almacenar material biológico y datos para investigaciones futuras?
reference: Free and informed consent must be obtained for the collection, processing, storage and foreseeable secondary use of biological material and identifiable or re-identifiable data; storage for multiple and indefinite uses should follow the WMA Declaration of Taipei; a research ethics committee must approve the establishment and monitor the use of such databases and biobanks; where consent is impossible or impracticable, secondary research may be done only after consideration and approval by a research ethics committee (Declaration of Helsinki 2024 ¶32).

question_en: Does the Declaration of Helsinki require compensation for participants harmed by research?
question_es: ¿Exige la Declaración de Helsinki compensar a los participantes que sufran daños por la investigación?
reference: Yes: appropriate compensation and treatment for participants who are harmed as a result of participating in research must be ensured (Declaration of Helsinki 2024 ¶15).
